items.front: Five dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate in order?
items.back: Slave/Mamluk (1206) → Khalji (1290) → Tughlaq (1320) → Sayyid (1414) → Lodi (1451-1526).
items.examPoint: Five dynasties of the Delhi Sultanate — sequence & dates (1206–1526)
items.source: notes

items.front: Which battles founded Turkish rule; who lost Chandawar (1194)?
items.back: Tarain 1191/1192 (Ghuri vs Prithviraj) + Chandawar 1194 defeated Jaichandra of Kannauj.
items.examPoint: Ghurid conquest — Muhammad Ghuri, Tarain (1191/1192) & Chandawar (1194)
items.source: notes

items.front: First Sultan of Delhi, called 'Lakh Baksh', who began the Qutb Minar?
items.back: Qutb-ud-din Aibak; also built the Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque.
items.examPoint: Slave/Mamluk Dynasty & Qutb-ud-din Aibak (Lakh Baksh, Qutb Minar)
items.source: notes

items.front: Sultan who issued the silver tanka and organised the iqta system?
items.back: Iltutmish; also set up the Chihalgani and shifted the capital to Delhi.
items.examPoint: Iltutmish — iqta system, silver tanka, Chihalgani, capital to Delhi
items.source: notes

items.front: First and only woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate?
items.back: Razia Sultana (1236-40), daughter of Iltutmish.
items.examPoint: Razia Sultana — first woman Muslim ruler of Delhi
items.source: notes

items.front: Balban's court practices exalting the king?
items.back: Sijda (prostration) & paibos (kissing feet); Zill-i-Ilahi ideal; broke the Chihalgani.
items.examPoint: Balban — blood-and-iron policy, sijda & paibos, breaking the Chihalgani
items.source: notes

items.front: Who led Alauddin Khalji's Deccan raids, and against which four powers?
items.back: Malik Kafur — Devagiri (Yadava), Warangal (Kakatiya), Dwarasamudra (Hoysala), Madurai (Pandya).
items.examPoint: Alauddin Khalji — Deccan campaigns under Malik Kafur (Devagiri, Warangal, Dwarasamudra, Madurai)
items.source: notes

items.front: Which Sultan introduced market/price-control regulations?
items.back: Alauddin Khalji — mandi, Sarai Adl, Shahna-i-Mandi supervisor, Diwan-i-Riyasat registry.
items.examPoint: Alauddin Khalji — market & price-control reforms
items.source: notes

items.front: Alauddin's military checks Dagh and Chehra?
items.back: Dagh = branding of horses; Chehra = descriptive roll of soldiers; first cash-paid standing army.
items.examPoint: Alauddin Khalji — military reforms (standing army, Dagh & Chehra)
items.source: notes

items.front: Which Sultan transferred the capital to Daulatabad and issued token currency?
items.back: Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq; both failed. Ibn Battuta served as his qazi.
items.examPoint: Muhammad-bin-Tughlaq — Daulatabad capital transfer & token currency
items.source: notes

items.front: Which Sultan dug canals, built welfare bodies and levied jizya on Brahmins?
items.back: Firoz Shah Tughlaq; wrote Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi; brought two Ashokan pillars to Delhi.
items.examPoint: Firoz Shah Tughlaq — canals, welfare works, jizya on Brahmins
items.source: notes

items.front: Who sacked Delhi in 1398, and who founded the Sayyid dynasty (1414)?
items.back: Timur sacked Delhi (1398); Khizr Khan founded the Sayyid dynasty (1414).
items.examPoint: Timur's invasion of Delhi (1398)
items.source: notes

items.front: First Afghan dynasty of Delhi; who founded Agra; who fell at Panipat 1526?
items.back: Lodis — Bahlol (founder), Sikandar (founded Agra, 1504), Ibrahim (lost to Babur, 1526).
items.examPoint: Lodi dynasty — Bahlol, Sikandar (Agra) & Ibrahim; First Battle of Panipat 1526
items.source: notes

items.front: What was the iqta, and India's first true dome/arch?
items.back: Iqta = non-hereditary revenue assignment to muqtis for troops; Alai Darwaza (1311) = first true dome.
items.examPoint: Delhi Sultanate architecture — Indo-Islamic (Qutb Minar, Alai Darwaza, Lodi tombs)
items.source: notes

items.front: Who wrote the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi, and who wrote the Rihla?
items.back: Ziauddin Barani (Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi); Ibn Battuta (Rihla). Minhaj = Tabaqat-i-Nasiri.
items.examPoint: Literary sources & chroniclers — Amir Khusrau, Barani, Minhaj-us-Siraj, Ibn Battuta
items.source: notes

items.back: Adhai — Aibak built the Adhai-din-ka-Jhonpra at Ajmer.
